questions.stem: What is 'eine Patchworkfamilie'?
options: A family that has often moved between countries
A family in which both parents work part-time
A blended family from earlier relationships
A large family with several generations under one roof
questions.explanation: A 'Patchworkfamilie' joins parents and children from earlier relationships, like patches sewn together. Several generations under one roof is 'die Großfamilie'.

questions.stem: What does 'Meine Mutter ist alleinerziehend' mean?
options: My mother is the only child in her family
My mother has lived alone since we moved out
My mother teaches her children at home
My mother is raising her children on her own
questions.explanation: 'Alleinerziehend' combines 'allein' (alone) and 'erziehen' (to bring up): a single parent. It says nothing about schooling at home, which is not generally allowed in Germany.

questions.stem: What is 'die Elternzeit'?
options: The age at which most people become parents
An evening when parents meet the teachers
Parental leave after a child is born
The time parents spend helping at school events
questions.explanation: 'Elternzeit' is parental leave: time off work to care for a young child, which mothers and fathers can both take. A meeting with teachers is 'der Elternabend' or 'der Elternsprechtag'.

questions.stem: Read: 'Bei uns ist mein Vater Hausmann, und meine Mutter verdient das Geld.' What does the writer describe?
options: A father who works from home for a company
A mother who gave up her job for the family
A reversal of the traditional roles in a family
A family in which both parents work full-time
questions.explanation: A 'Hausmann' is a house husband who runs the home, while the mother is the earner. That turns the stereotypical roles around. Working from home is 'im Homeoffice arbeiten'.

questions.stem: In a discussion about families, what does 'traditionelle Rollenbilder' refer to?
options: Photographs of the family kept for generations
Famous people whom children look up to
Old customs for family celebrations
Fixed ideas about what men and women should do
questions.explanation: 'Rollenbilder' are images of roles: expectations about who earns, cooks or cares for children. A person you look up to is 'ein Vorbild', which is a different word.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Die Rolle ___ Frau hat sich in den letzten Jahrzehnten stark verändert.'?
options: dem
des
der
die
questions.explanation: 'Of the woman' needs the genitive, and the feminine genitive article is 'der'. 'Des' is the genitive for masculine and neuter nouns, as in 'die Rolle des Vaters'.

questions.stem: Which form completes 'Mein ___ Großvater wohnt seit letztem Jahr bei uns.' ('old')?
options: alter
alte
alten
altes
questions.explanation: 'Mein' has no ending in the masculine nominative, so the adjective shows the gender with '-er': 'mein alter Großvater'. After 'der' it would be 'der alte Großvater'.

questions.stem: Which phrase completes 'Heute wachsen viele Kinder in ___ auf.' ('small families')?
options: kleine Familien
kleiner Familien
kleinen Familie
kleinen Familien
questions.explanation: 'In' here gives a location, so it takes the dative. With no article, the adjective takes the strong dative plural ending '-en', and the plural noun is 'Familien'.

questions.stem: What does 'das geschiedene Ehepaar' mean?
options: The separated twins
The divorced couple
The newly married couple
The engaged couple
questions.explanation: 'Geschieden' is the participle of 'scheiden' (to divorce), used here as an adjective. An engaged couple is 'das verlobte Paar'.

questions.stem: Who is 'der Halbbruder'?
options: The husband of your sister
A boy who joins your family as a foster child
A brother who shares only one parent with you
A brother who is much younger than you
questions.explanation: A half-brother has one parent in common with you. Your sister's husband is 'der Schwager', and a stepbrother ('der Stiefbruder') shares no parent with you.

questions.stem: Read: 'In Deutschland betreuen viele Großeltern ihre Enkel, wenn beide Eltern arbeiten.' What role do the grandparents play?
options: They look after the grandchildren while the parents work
They pay for their grandchildren's education
They live with the family and do the housework
They visit only during the school holidays
questions.explanation: 'Betreuen' means to look after, and the 'wenn' clause gives the situation: when both parents are at work. Nothing is said about money or living together.

questions.stem: Read: 'Zwar sehe ich meine Cousins nur zweimal im Jahr, aber wir schreiben uns fast täglich.' What does the speaker say?
options: They meet rarely but stay in touch almost every day
They write rarely because they meet so often
They see each other twice a week and write daily
They lost contact after the cousins moved away
questions.explanation: 'Zwar ... aber' sets a concession against a contrast: they meet only twice a year ('zweimal im Jahr'), but they message almost daily. 'Zweimal in der Woche' would be twice a week.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Er ist sehr stolz ___ seine Tochter.'?
options: für
auf
von
über
questions.explanation: 'Stolz' is used with 'auf' plus the accusative: 'stolz auf jemanden sein'. English 'proud of' tempts students towards 'von', which does not go with this adjective.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Viele Jugendliche sind finanziell noch von ___ Eltern abhängig.'?
options: ihre
ihrer
ihr
ihren
questions.explanation: 'Abhängig von' (dependent on) takes 'von', which always takes the dative. The dative plural of 'ihre' is 'ihren'.

questions.stem: What does 'Ich habe mich mit Lena fürs Kino verabredet' mean?
options: I apologised to Lena for the cinema
I arranged to see a film with Lena
I said goodbye to Lena at the cinema
I argued with Lena about the cinema
questions.explanation: 'Sich verabreden' means to arrange to meet someone. Saying goodbye is 'sich verabschieden', which looks similar.

questions.stem: A German teenager says 'Das ist mein Freund Jonas.' Why might listeners think Jonas is her boyfriend?
options: 'Freund' is used only for friendships between adults
German uses 'Freund' only for people of the same age
'Mein Freund' often means a partner; 'ein Freund von mir' does not
Adding a first name after 'Freund' always marks a partner
questions.explanation: 'Mein Freund' or 'meine Freundin' usually suggests a romantic partner. To make clear someone is just a friend, Germans say 'ein Freund von mir' or 'ein guter Freund'.

questions.stem: What does 'Wir haben uns aus den Augen verloren' mean?
options: We lost touch with each other
We stopped looking at each other
We have not seen each other today
We disagreed about everything
questions.explanation: The idiom literally says 'we lost each other from our eyes': the friendship faded and contact stopped. It is not about a single day.

questions.stem: What does the saying 'Freunde erkennt man in der Not' mean?
options: Real friends show up when you are in trouble
Friends are easy to recognise in a large crowd
You should never ask your friends for help
Friends made in hard times never last
questions.explanation: 'Die Not' is need or hardship. The saying matches 'a friend in need is a friend indeed': you find out who your real friends are when things go badly.

questions.stem: What does 'sich zum Affen machen' mean?
options: To make a fool of yourself
To lose your temper
To behave cheekily to adults
To copy what others do
questions.explanation: Literally 'to make yourself into a monkey', it means to look ridiculous. Copying others is 'nachäffen', a different verb.

questions.stem: Read: 'In Deutschland lernen sich viele Jugendliche im Sportverein kennen, nicht nur in der Schule.' What does this say?
options: Sports clubs in Germany are mainly for adults
Clubs outside school are a common place to make friends
Most friendships begin in school sports teams in Germany
Young people rarely play sport after school
questions.explanation: 'Nicht nur in der Schule' points outside school: the 'Verein' (club) is a big part of social life. School teams are much less common in Germany than in Australia.

questions.stem: Read: 'Online-Freundschaften sind praktisch, doch sie ersetzen kein echtes Treffen. Wer nur chattet, merkt nicht, wenn es dem anderen schlecht geht.' What is the writer's view?
options: Online contact is useful but cannot replace meeting in person
Online friends are more honest than friends at school
Chatting makes it easier to notice when friends are sad
Meeting friends in person has become old-fashioned
questions.explanation: 'Praktisch, doch ... ersetzen kein echtes Treffen' concedes a benefit, then limits it. The second sentence says chatting hides how a friend really feels, the opposite of noticing more.

questions.stem: What does 'Am Wochenende hänge ich meistens mit meinen Freunden ab' mean?
options: At the weekend I usually avoid my friends
At the weekend I mostly say goodbye to friends
At the weekend I mostly hang out with friends
At the weekend I mostly depend on my friends
questions.explanation: Colloquial 'abhängen' (separable, with 'mit') means to hang out. 'Abhängen von' or 'abhängig sein von' means to depend on, which needs 'von'.

questions.stem: Which sentence has correct word order?
options: Obwohl mag ich meine Freunde, ich brauche manchmal Zeit für mich.
Obwohl ich meine Freunde mag, brauche ich manchmal Zeit für mich.
Obwohl ich mag meine Freunde, brauche ich manchmal Zeit für mich.
Obwohl ich meine Freunde mag, ich brauche manchmal Zeit für mich.
questions.explanation: 'Obwohl' sends its verb to the end of its clause ('mag'). The whole clause then fills first place, so the main verb 'brauche' comes straight after the comma, before 'ich'.

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Ich weiß nicht, ___ sie heute Abend mitkommt.' ('whether')?
options: wenn
dass
falls
ob
questions.explanation: 'Ob' introduces an indirect yes/no question: whether. English 'if' tempts students to use 'wenn', but 'wenn' means 'if' only in conditions ('if it rains').

questions.stem: Which word completes 'Ruf mich an, ___ du Hilfe brauchst.' ('in case')?
options: ob
damit
indem
falls
questions.explanation: 'Falls' means in case or if. 'Damit' means so that, and 'indem' means by doing something.

questions.stem: A student in Germany has a '5' in maths on her report. What does this mean?
options: Her work is 'mangelhaft', a failing mark
Her work is 'sehr gut', the top mark
Her work is 'befriedigend', a middle mark
She missed five maths lessons this term
questions.explanation: German schools mark from 1 ('sehr gut') to 6 ('ungenügend'). A 4 ('ausreichend') is the lowest pass, so 5 ('mangelhaft') is a fail.

questions.stem: Which statement about school marks in German-speaking countries is correct?
options: In Switzerland 1 is the best mark, just as in Germany
Germany, Austria and Switzerland all use letters A to E
In Switzerland 6 is the best mark, but in Germany it is the worst
In Austria and Germany 6 is the best mark, and 1 the worst
questions.explanation: Swiss schools count upwards, with 6 the best and 4 a pass. Germany runs from 1 (best) to 6, and Austria from 1 (best) to 5.

questions.stem: What does 'sitzenbleiben' mean at school?
options: To stay back after class as a punishment
To remain seated when the teacher enters
To skip a year and move ahead
To repeat a school year
questions.explanation: A student who 'bleibt sitzen' is not moved up ('nicht versetzt') and repeats the year. Detention is 'nachsitzen', which looks similar.

questions.stem: What is 'das Zeugnis'?
options: A school report with a student's marks
A written test done in class
A permission slip signed for an excursion
A certificate for full attendance
questions.explanation: The 'Zeugnis' is the report given at the end of a term or year, with a mark in each subject. A test written in class is 'die Klassenarbeit'.

questions.stem: What is 'die Ganztagsschule'?
options: A school where lessons and activities go on into the afternoon
A school that runs on Saturdays as well as on weekdays
A boarding school where students live all year round
A school for students who work during the day
questions.explanation: Traditionally many German schools finished around lunchtime, and students ate at home. A 'Ganztagsschule' keeps students into the afternoon, with lunch, homework help and activities.

questions.stem: Which statement compares school life in Germany and Australia accurately?
options: Most German schools require a blazer and tie
The German school year starts in late January each year
German students choose a school type at 16
Most German students do not wear a school uniform
questions.explanation: Uniforms are rare in German schools, unlike in Australia. The German school year starts in late summer (August or September), and the choice of secondary school usually comes after Year 4.

questions.stem: After the 'Grundschule', which type of secondary school is the academic one that leads to the Abitur?
options: die Realschule
die Berufsschule
die Hauptschule
das Gymnasium
questions.explanation: The 'Gymnasium' is the academic secondary school, ending with the Abitur. It is a false friend: a sports hall is 'die Turnhalle'. The 'Berufsschule' is the vocational college attended alongside an apprenticeship.

questions.stem: What is 'eine Klassenfahrt'?
options: A class trip, often lasting several days
The bus that takes students to school
A change of class at the start of the year
A class debate about a current issue
questions.explanation: A 'Klassenfahrt' is a trip away with the class and teachers, often for several days. The school bus is 'der Schulbus'.

questions.stem: What does 'Heute haben wir hitzefrei!' mean?
options: School is closed today for a public holiday
School lets us go home early because of the heat
We have a free lesson because the teacher is ill
We have outdoor sport today because it is warm
questions.explanation: 'Hitzefrei' means time off because of heat: students are sent home early on very hot days. A cancelled lesson is 'eine Freistunde'.

questions.stem: What is 'die Schulpflicht' in Germany?
options: Compulsory school attendance for all children
The duty to wear a uniform at school every day
The rule that students must do homework
A school's duty to provide free lunches
questions.explanation: 'Die Pflicht' is a duty, so 'Schulpflicht' is compulsory schooling. In Germany children must attend a school, and home schooling is generally not allowed.

questions.stem: Read: 'Das Schöne an der Schule ist, dass man jeden Tag seine Freunde sieht. Der Stress vor den Klassenarbeiten ist aber manchmal zu viel.' What does the student say?
options: Seeing friends is good, but test stress is sometimes too much
Tests are easy, but she rarely sees her friends at school
She enjoys tests because she can compare marks with friends
The stress comes from her friends rather than from tests
questions.explanation: 'Das Schöne' (the good thing) is seeing friends daily; 'aber' introduces the challenge, stress before 'Klassenarbeiten' (class tests). The text weighs a benefit against a challenge.

questions.stem: What does 'Wir müssen ein Referat über Goethe halten' mean?
options: We have to visit Goethe's house in Weimar
We have to give a presentation on Goethe
We have to write a class test on Goethe
We have to read a whole book by Goethe
questions.explanation: 'Ein Referat halten' is to give a talk or presentation in class. A written test is 'eine Klassenarbeit schreiben'.

questions.stem: What does 'Je mehr ich lerne, desto besser werden meine Noten' mean?
options: I study more than I need to for good marks
My marks were better when I studied more
Even when I study, my marks do not improve
The more I study, the better my marks get
questions.explanation: 'Je ... desto' links two comparatives: the more ..., the better .... The 'je' clause has its verb at the end, and the 'desto' clause has the verb straight after the comparative.

questions.stem: In an essay, what does 'im Vergleich zu' introduce, as in 'Im Vergleich zu meiner alten Schule ist diese Schule viel größer'?
options: A conclusion to the paragraph
A comparison with something else
A reason for the point that follows
An example of the previous point
questions.explanation: 'Im Vergleich zu' means compared with, a cohesive device for comparisons. A reason would use 'weil' or 'denn', and an example 'zum Beispiel'.

questions.stem: What does the abbreviation 'd.h.' stand for in a German text?
options: das heißt (that is)
die Hälfte (half)
durch Hilfe (with help)
der Hauptpunkt (main point)
questions.explanation: 'D.h.' is 'das heißt', used like English 'i.e.'. Other common abbreviations are 'z.B.' (zum Beispiel), 'usw.' (und so weiter) and 'bzw.' (beziehungsweise).
